site: Sheep Mountain Anticline, Bighorn Basin, Wyoming, USA
source: USGS State Geologic Map Compilation (SGMC, Horton et al., 2017) / Wyoming State Geological Survey (Love & Christiansen, 1985)

units.name: Madison Limestone
units.lithology: Massive marine limestone and cherty dolostone forming the inner gorge and anticlinal core

units.name: Tensleep Sandstone & Amsden Fm
units.lithology: Cross-bedded eolian quartzose sandstone, cherty dolostone, and basal red shale

units.name: Chugwater & Goose Egg Fms
units.lithology: Ferric-oxide-rich red siltstone, mudstone, fine sandstone, thin carbonate, and evaporitic gypsum

units.name: Sundance & Gypsum Spring Fms
units.lithology: Glauconitic marine sandstone, greenish-gray calcareous shale, oolitic limestone, and basal gypsum

units.name: Cloverly & Morrison Fms
units.lithology: Resistant chert-pebble conglomerate and quartz sandstone hogbacks over variegated claystone

units.name: Mowry & Thermopolis Shales
units.lithology: Siliceous silver-gray fish-scale shale, bentonite beds, and dark marine mudstone

units.name: Quaternary Alluvium & Terrace
units.lithology: Unconsolidated Bighorn River floodplain sand, silt, gravel, and pediment fan deposits
